root.name: Queen's Pawn Game: Veresov, Richter Attack

overview: White supports an e4 break with f3 and Nc3, a Blackmar-Diemer-flavoured set-up without the gambit pawn. I am unsure of the exact theory. Black can answer with ...c5, ...e6 or ...e5, and White follows with e4 for a broad centre at the cost of a weakened kingside and slower development.

white_ideas.idea: Play e4 for a big centre, supported by f3.
Develop with Be3, Qd2 and queenside castling.

black_ideas.idea: Strike at the centre with ...c5 or ...e5 before e4 is played.
Develop quickly and punish the f3 weakness.

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4/f3 centre against ...e6/...c5 or ...e5 counters.

character.notes: Slightly loosened king position but White has no direct threats.

gambit.notes: No material given in the main replies, though ...dxe4 fxe4 lines resemble BDG.

soundness.notes: Playable but probably slightly inferior for White.

structure.notes: Centre fluid, depending on Black's counter.

approach.notes: Rare, seldom chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Little theory; plans are clear but easy to misjudge.

character.reason: Unsure; quiet development with a slight king-safety risk.

level.reason: Not much theory but easy to misplay.

plans.reason: White aims at e4 with a big centre.
